course: Middle-school physical science, grade 6: matter, mixtures and measuring what is in water
curriculum: Everything is made of matter, and matter comes in solids, liquids and gases
A mixture is things sharing a space without becoming one another
Dissolving, and why some things dissolve and others do not
Concentration: how much of something is in how much of everything
Dilution: adding water lowers the concentration and not the amount
Separating a mixture, using a difference between the parts
Weight is conserved: what goes in has to come out somewhere
Measuring the same thing several times, and averaging
A blank and a standard: how a laboratory knows a number is real
A sample stands for a place and a moment, and only those
A limit is a number somebody chose, for a reason worth knowing
Acids and bases, and why the middle is where things are stable
Reactions give out heat or take it in, and heat speeds things up
Gases spread out, and the wind decides where
A treatment can move a problem rather than remove it
Saying what you know and how well you know it

groups.name: Molecular Identification
groups.desc: Composition, charge, separation and spectra — what the material in the containers actually is.

groups.name: Atmosphere & Gases
groups.desc: Gas laws, plume behaviour, photochemistry — how the release moves and changes in air.

groups.name: Solutions & Water Chemistry
groups.desc: Polarity, partitioning, pH and equilibrium — where the contaminant goes once it is wet.

groups.name: Quantitative Analysis
groups.desc: Dilution, calibration, detection limits and uncertainty — turning a signal into a defensible number.

groups.name: Reactions & Energy
groups.desc: Stoichiometry, calorimetry and kinetics — how much can react, how much heat, and how fast.

groups.name: Treatment & Infrastructure
groups.desc: Corrosion, treatment trains, byproducts and the long tail — fixing it without making it worse.
